title: Explosion Rocks Bulgarian Defense Facility in Latest Arms Depot Blast
snippet: Bulgarian officials have launched a high-level investigation after an explosion struck a weapons facility owned by defense manufacturer EMCO, the latest in a series of mysterious blasts hitting the country's arms sector.
content:
SOFIA, Bulgaria — Bulgarian authorities have launched a formal investigation after a powerful explosion struck a weapons facility owned by defense manufacturer EMCO, state officials confirmed.

Emergency personnel rushed to the scene following reports of the detonation at the site. While initial reports indicate no casualties were sustained, the blast caused substantial structural damage. First responders established a secure perimeter around the location to prevent secondary detonations and allow investigators to assess the scene safely.

A Pattern of Suspicious Incidents

This latest blast is part of a troubling series of unexplained explosions that have targeted Bulgarian munitions depots and arms production plants over the past decade. EMCO, owned by prominent defense contractor Emilian Gebrev, has been targeted in multiple past incidents. Gebrev notably survived a 2015 nerve-agent poisoning attempt that Western intelligence agencies later connected to Russian operatives.

In recent years, Bulgarian prosecutors have actively investigated potential links between foreign intelligence agencies and explosions at facilities housing ammunition intended for export to strategic international partners, including Ukraine.

Probe Underway

Law enforcement and national security agencies have not yet named suspects or publicly declared a definitive cause, stating that all possibilities—ranging from industrial accidents to deliberate sabotage—are currently being evaluated.

Forensic teams are scheduled to conduct a detailed sweep of the site once safety officials confirm that the risk of unexploded ordnance has been fully mitigated.
